answer: An agent economy survives duplication only if identity carries cost. Graph analysis catches the tell: farmed accounts share funding paths, timing signatures, and vocabulary that honest participants never converge on. Think of it as a pigment the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single ledge of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a signal of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
